name: TX-33
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+18 partisan lean strongly favors Democrats
Colin Allred is a well-funded, high-profile nominee with $7.4M raised
Prediction markets price Democratic win at roughly 96%
Open seat removes incumbency but not the underlying lean
model.rationale: The district's D+18 lean and the fundamentals point to a comfortable Democratic hold, and Allred's fundraising and name recognition only reinforce that. Markets price a Democratic win near certain, so the seat stays Safe D despite the open-seat transition.
model.watch: A major polling surprise or an unexpectedly strong Republican environment in Texas could narrow the margin, though a flip remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jasmine Crockett (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Jasmine Crockett is leaving the seat to run for Senate, but Democrats are positioned to hold this Dallas-area district with ease. The seat leans Democratic by 18 points, and former Senate nominee Colin Allred enters the race as a strong, well-known candidate who has raised over $7.4 million. Republican Patrick Gillespie has reported little fundraising and faces steep structural disadvantages.

Prediction markets give Democrats roughly a 96 percent chance of holding the seat, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. The main uncertainty is the size of the margin rather than the winner, with the open-seat transition the only mild source of risk.
